excluded: out-of-order FIN buffering and FIN carrying payload
RTT/Karn, delayed ACK, complete persist, congestion/recovery

CONN-OPEN.interpretation: Select ISS; active OPEN enters SYN-SENT, passive OPEN enters LISTEN.

CONN-LISTEN.interpretation: A SYN in LISTEN initializes receive state and emits SYN+ACK; ACK-bearing input emits RST; RST is ignored.

CONN-SYN-SENT.interpretation: Validate ACK before processing SYN/RST; valid SYN+ACK establishes, bare SYN enters SYN-RECEIVED.

CONN-SIMULTANEOUS.interpretation: Figure 7: active vs passive origin is retained in SYN-RECEIVED; simultaneous SYN+ACK completes synchronization.

CONN-ACK.interpretation: In-order ACK completes synchronization or acknowledges FIN, with per-state transitions.

CONN-FIN.interpretation: FIN consumes one receive sequence number, is acknowledged, and changes per-state close progression.

CONN-CLOSE.interpretation: CLOSE in ESTABLISHED or CLOSE-WAIT emits FIN and enters FIN-WAIT-1 or LAST-ACK; repeated close does not emit a second FIN.

CONN-ABORT.interpretation: ABORT sends RST in the specified synchronized states; other states discard the TCB without output RST.

CONN-RESET.interpretation: Exact RCV.NXT resets the connection; passive SYN-RECEIVED returns to LISTEN, active origin closes.

CONN-CLOSED-INPUT.interpretation: CLOSED ignores resets and emits a correctly formatted reset for other control segments.

CONN-TIMEOUT.interpretation: User timeout deletes the TCB; retransmission timeout repeats oldest outstanding segment; TIME-WAIT timeout closes.

RTO-PROFILE.interpretation: Use 1000ms initial SYN RTO and exponential doubling for control retransmission. After a SYN timeout use at least 3000ms for subsequent FIN, retaining a larger backed-off value; no RTT estimator is modeled.

CONNECTION-PROFILE.interpretation: Inherited single-connection control paths retain validated control shapes, exact sequence checks and configurable user/MSL deadlines. The data extension supersedes the base zero-payload assumption only in ESTABLISHED, within the explicit DATA-SCOPE boundary; data in other lifecycle states remains excluded.

DATA-SEQ.interpretation: Each new data octet consumes one sequence number; cumulative ACK removes an acknowledged prefix. Retransmission does not advance SND.NXT.

DATA-ACK.interpretation: New ACKs satisfy SND.UNA < SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT; duplicate and old ACKs do not remove data; future ACK triggers an ACK.

DATA-WINDOW.interpretation: Update SND.WND only for acceptable ACK and newer WL1/WL2. Segmentation respects the available advertised send window.

DATA-RECEIVE.interpretation: Accept and trim text overlapping the receive window; advance RCV.NXT only over contiguous newly accepted bytes, ACK the next expected octet.

DATA-SEND.interpretation: Model buffers application octets and segments them within the configured capacity, MSS and send window.

DATA-RTX.interpretation: The retransmission timer sends the oldest outstanding data again. This profile uses fixed initial RTO and exponential backoff only.

DATA-RTO.interpretation: Start on first outstanding transmission, restart on new partial ACK, cancel on all acknowledged, retransmit oldest on expiry and double RTO (5.1-5.6). No RTT sampling or maximum retry policy.

DATA-SCOPE.interpretation: Inherit finite buffers/connection and explicit reassembly, expand accepted ACK+payload/window composition and shrinking windows; first accepted byte wins, raw accepted SEG.SEQ used for WL1. Only ESTABLISHED, no FIN data or full recovery/persist implementation.

RX-QUEUE.interpretation: Retain higher sequence-number payload in the finite receive window (SHLD-31); process the entire contiguous queued prefix before one ACK (MUST-59).

RX-WINDOW.interpretation: Apply Table 6 nonempty-payload acceptability: positive receive window and first or last payload sequence within the offered interval. Trim accepted data to that interval.

RX-SEQUENCE.interpretation: Advance RCV.NXT only by contiguous newly accepted octets, modulo 2^32, with no repeated application delivery.

RX-SCOPE.interpretation: Inherit finite buffers/connection and explicit reassembly, expand accepted ACK+payload/window composition and shrinking windows; first accepted byte wins, raw accepted SEG.SEQ used for WL1. Only ESTABLISHED, no FIN data or full recovery/persist implementation.

SEG-ORDER.interpretation: Validate receive sequence first; reject unacceptable segments before ACK/window processing; process ACK/window before text. Future ACK causes ACK+drop; old ACK does not discard accepted payload.

SEG-ACK.interpretation: Cumulative ACK removes acknowledged retransmission prefix. Full ACK cancels rtx, new partial ACK restarts it, duplicate/old ACK leaves its deadline. ACK-only valid segments do not cause ACK loops.

SEG-WINDOW.interpretation: Update advertised peer window only for SND.UNA <= SEG.ACK <= SND.NXT with fresh WL1/WL2; SEG.SEQ uses the original accepted wire header in this profile.

SEG-SHRINK.interpretation: Sender remains robust when the usable window becomes negative (MUST-34). No new data is sent beyond the current window; retransmit oldest outstanding data within the positive window (SHLD-15/16).

SEG-ZERO-FLIGHT.interpretation: With outstanding data and zero peer window, the existing timeout sends one oldest octet as a probe and backs off. Zero window with only unsent data still requires the later persist mechanism.

SEG-SCOPE.interpretation: Inherit finite buffers/connection and explicit reassembly, expand accepted ACK+payload/window composition and shrinking windows; first accepted byte wins, raw accepted SEG.SEQ used for WL1. Only ESTABLISHED, no FIN data or full recovery/persist implementation.

CL-QUEUE.interpretation: Queue CLOSE after preceding SENDs are segmentized. Active close enters FIN-WAIT-1 immediately. FIN consumes one sequence number after data; repeat close must not consume another.

CL-ACK.interpretation: Process ACK before text/FIN, remove acknowledged data prefix and independently acknowledge FIN. FIN-WAIT-1 advances only when its FIN is acknowledged; CLOSING then enters TIME-WAIT, LAST-ACK enters CLOSED.

CL-HALF.interpretation: Read previously accepted data through half-close; receive text during FIN-WAIT-1/2. Peer FIN does not erase outstanding local data; CLOSE-WAIT can still send before local close.

CL-TIMER.interpretation: Data and FIN share one retransmission timer; preserve its deadline when adding FIN to an existing flight. Partial ACK restarts, full ACK cancels. Retransmit oldest data before FIN without consuming sequence space.

CL-SCOPE.interpretation: Finite 16-octet queues; separate FIN-only event with implicit unchanged peer window. Out-of-order FIN is ACKed/dropped and must be retransmitted; FIN+payload and no-flight persist remain pending. app.transmit explicitly schedules queued bytes/FIN.
